providers.name: ERGO NEXT (formerly NEXT Insurance)
providers.tagline: Digital small-business insurer, renamed ERGO NEXT in 2026 and owned by Munich Re's ERGO, selling general liability, BOP, workers' comp and professional liability online and through agents
providers.quote_speed: Online quote and purchase; ERGO NEXT says buying and servicing are available 24/7
providers.typical_premium_range: Quoted per business
providers.states_note: ERGO NEXT says it covers small businesses nationwide; confirm during the quote that each line you need is offered for your trade in your state
providers.headquartered: Palo Alto, CA (part of ERGO, Munich Re's primary insurance group, since July 2025)
providers.long_description:
ERGO NEXT Insurance, called NEXT Insurance until January 2026, is a digital insurer for small businesses, including contractors and other trade businesses. NEXT was founded in 2016 and is based in Palo Alto, California. Munich Re announced the deal to buy NEXT in March 2025, and ERGO, Munich Re's primary insurance group, completed the full acquisition on July 1, 2025, at a valuation of $2.6 billion for 100 percent of the shares (ERGO already held about 29 percent). The company took the ERGO NEXT Insurance name on January 15, 2026.

ERGO NEXT describes its product as simple, digital coverage for small business owners. Its current company description lists general liability, business owner's policies (BOP), workers' compensation and professional liability, plus other coverages it does not name there. NEXT's 2025 company description says customers get 24/7 access to purchasing and servicing, including certificates of insurance and adding additional insureds, with no extra fees. ERGO NEXT says it serves more than 750,000 small business customers.

NEXT is not only an online seller. It also works with independent insurance agencies, and in January 2026 it launched a recognition program for its agency partners with profit-sharing and advance commissions. A contractor can buy directly online, or through an independent agent who places business with ERGO NEXT.

The trade-off: premiums come only from a quote, and buying online without an agent puts the coverage choices on you. Compare the ERGO NEXT quote with at least one agent-shopped quote, and check that the limits, additional insured wording and any commercial auto or tools coverage you need are on the policy before you pay.
providers.how_it_works: Start a quote on the ERGO NEXT website, pick your type of business, answer questions about the business and the coverage you want, and review the price. Policies can be bought online, and ERGO NEXT says purchasing and servicing are available 24/7, including certificates of insurance and adding additional insureds with no extra fees. If you would rather have advice, ERGO NEXT also sells through independent insurance agencies. Confirm during the quote which lines are offered for your trade and state, and read the limits and exclusions before you pay.

pros_detail.title: Buy and manage coverage online
pros_detail.explanation: ERGO NEXT sells policies online and says purchasing and servicing are available 24/7, so you can get a quote and buy outside an agent's office hours.

pros_detail.title: Certificates of insurance with no extra fees
pros_detail.explanation: NEXT's company description says online servicing includes certificates of insurance and adding additional insureds, with no extra fees. That matters for trades that must send proof of insurance to general contractors and property managers.

pros_detail.title: Part of the Munich Re group
pros_detail.explanation: ERGO, Munich Re's primary insurance group, completed its acquisition of NEXT on July 1, 2025.

pros_detail.title: Core small-business lines from one carrier
pros_detail.explanation: ERGO NEXT lists general liability, business owner's policies, workers' compensation and professional liability, so a small shop can keep its main policies with one company.

pros_detail.title: Direct or through an agent
pros_detail.explanation: Besides selling online, ERGO NEXT works with independent insurance agencies and launched a recognition program for them in January 2026, so you can still use an agent if you want advice.

cons_detail.title: No published prices
cons_detail.explanation: Premiums come only from a quote, so the only way to know whether ERGO NEXT is competitive for your trade is to compare its quote with others.

cons_detail.title: Self-service puts the coverage choices on you
cons_detail.explanation: Buying online without an agent means you choose limits, endorsements and exclusions yourself. Read the policy before you buy, or use an agent if you are unsure what your contracts require.

cons_detail.title: Check each line for your trade and state
cons_detail.explanation: The lines ERGO NEXT names in its company description are general liability, BOP, workers' compensation and professional liability. If you also need commercial auto, tools and equipment or umbrella coverage, confirm during the quote that it is offered for your trade and state.

cons_detail.title: Large or unusual risks may need a specialist
cons_detail.explanation: ERGO NEXT focuses on small businesses. Contractors with large commercial projects, high limit requirements or big fleets may need an agent who can place coverage with other carriers.

cons_detail.title: New name on an existing company
cons_detail.explanation: NEXT Insurance became ERGO NEXT Insurance in January 2026, so older reviews, documents and emails may use the old name. It is the same company.

providers.best_for: Small trade businesses that want to buy general liability, a BOP, workers' comp or professional liability online and handle certificates of insurance themselves
providers.weaknesses: Premiums only by quote, the self-service model leaves coverage choices to you, and lines beyond general liability, BOP, workers' comp and professional liability need checking for your trade and state
providers.affiliate_payout_note: NEXT runs an affiliate program through Impact. We have no affiliate relationship with NEXT and earn nothing if you get a quote

provider_faqs.q: Is NEXT Insurance the same company as ERGO NEXT?
provider_faqs.a: Yes. NEXT Insurance changed its name to ERGO NEXT Insurance on January 15, 2026, after ERGO, Munich Re's primary insurance group, completed its full acquisition of NEXT on July 1, 2025. The company is still based in Palo Alto, California.

provider_faqs.q: What coverage can a contractor buy from ERGO NEXT?
provider_faqs.a: ERGO NEXT's company description lists general liability, business owner's policies (BOP), workers' compensation and professional liability, plus other coverages. Check during the quote which lines are available for your trade and state.

provider_faqs.q: Can I get a certificate of insurance without calling anyone?
provider_faqs.a: NEXT says its online servicing is available 24/7 and includes certificates of insurance and adding additional insureds, with no extra fees. Check that the certificate shows the limits and additional insured wording your customer asked for.

provider_faqs.q: How much does ERGO NEXT cost?
provider_faqs.a: ERGO NEXT quotes premiums per business, so the only way to know the price for your trade is to get a quote. Compare it with at least one other quote, for example from an independent agent, before you buy.

provider_faqs.q: What did the Munich Re acquisition change?
provider_faqs.a: NEXT became part of ERGO, Munich Re's primary insurance group. Munich Re announced the deal in March 2025, ERGO completed it on July 1, 2025 at a valuation of $2.6 billion, and the company took the ERGO NEXT name in January 2026.

providers.name: Hiscox
providers.tagline: Specialty insurer with Lloyd's roots going back to 1901, selling general liability, professional liability (E&O), BOP and cyber to US small businesses online and through brokers
providers.quote_speed: Online quote at hiscox.com (Hiscox advertises an instant quote) or through a broker
providers.typical_premium_range: Quoted per business
providers.states_note: Hiscox says its US insurance company insures customers anywhere in the country; confirm during the quote that the line you need is offered for your trade and state
providers.headquartered: Pembroke, Bermuda (Hiscox Ltd head office); US offices include Atlanta and New York
providers.long_description:
Hiscox is an international specialty insurance group listed on the London Stock Exchange. Its head office, Hiscox Ltd, is in Pembroke, Bermuda, and it has a large office in London. Hiscox says it traces its roots to 1901 in the Lloyd's market. It insured US customers through Lloyd's for many years before opening its own US insurance company in 2006, and it says it now works from ten US locations, including Atlanta, Chicago, Los Angeles, Miami and New York, and insures customers anywhere in the country.

For US small businesses, Hiscox sells general liability, professional liability (also called errors and omissions, or E&O), business owner's policies (BOP) and cyber insurance, and it has pages aimed at contractors and construction businesses. Hiscox says other coverage, such as workers' compensation, is available through partnerships with other carriers, so that part of your insurance would be written by a different company.

Hiscox sells both online and through brokers. On hiscox.com you enter your zip code and answer questions about your business to get a quote. Its contractor pages focus on professional and general liability, and Hiscox describes its professional liability as protection for contractors against claims of negligence, faulty workmanship and more.

The trade-off: the policies Hiscox writes itself center on liability, professional liability, BOP and cyber. A trade business that also needs workers' comp, commercial auto or tools coverage may end up with more than one insurer, and premiums come only from a quote, so compare Hiscox with a carrier or broker that can quote the whole program.
providers.how_it_works: Start a quote on hiscox.com by entering your zip code and answering questions about your business; Hiscox advertises an instant online quote. You can buy online or through a broker who places business with Hiscox. Hiscox writes general liability, professional liability, BOP and cyber itself; for workers' comp and some other coverage it offers policies from partner carriers. Before you buy, check the limits, additional insured options and exclusions against what your customers' contracts require.

pros_detail.title: Long history
pros_detail.explanation: Hiscox traces its roots to 1901 in the Lloyd's market.

pros_detail.title: Professional liability (E&O) for contractors
pros_detail.explanation: Hiscox sells professional liability alongside general liability and describes it as protecting contractors against claims of negligence and faulty workmanship. That is worth a look for design-build, inspection, consulting or project management work.

pros_detail.title: Buy online or through a broker
pros_detail.explanation: Hiscox says its small business insurance is available online or through brokers, so you can buy yourself or get advice from a broker.

pros_detail.title: BOP and cyber from the same insurer
pros_detail.explanation: Besides liability and E&O, Hiscox writes business owner's policies and cyber insurance, so an office-based or low-risk trade business can keep several policies with one company.

pros_detail.title: Nationwide US reach
pros_detail.explanation: Hiscox opened its own US insurance company in 2006 and says it insures customers anywhere in the country.

cons_detail.title: Workers' comp comes from partner carriers
cons_detail.explanation: Hiscox says coverage such as workers' compensation is available through partnerships with other carriers, so a shop with employees will deal with a second insurer for that policy.

cons_detail.title: No published prices
cons_detail.explanation: Premiums come only from a quote, so compare Hiscox's price with other carriers or a broker for the same limits.

cons_detail.title: Check vehicle and tools coverage
cons_detail.explanation: The lines Hiscox writes itself are general liability, professional liability, BOP and cyber. Shops that run vans or carry expensive tools should confirm how those risks would be covered and by which insurer.

cons_detail.title: Confirm your trade is written
cons_detail.explanation: Hiscox's contractor pages focus on professional and general liability. Confirm during the quote that Hiscox writes your specific trade and the limits your contracts require.

providers.best_for: Contractors and trade businesses that need professional liability (E&O) alongside general liability, a BOP or cyber coverage, and want to buy online or through a broker
providers.weaknesses: Workers' comp and some other coverage come from partner carriers, premiums only by quote, and trades with vehicles or large tool inventories need to check how those risks are covered
providers.affiliate_payout_note: ~$25 per qualified quote via Commission Junction, 30-day cookie

provider_faqs.q: Who is Hiscox?
provider_faqs.a: Hiscox is an international specialty insurance group listed on the London Stock Exchange, with its head office in Pembroke, Bermuda. It traces its roots to 1901 in the Lloyd's market and opened its own US insurance company in 2006.

provider_faqs.q: What coverage can a contractor buy from Hiscox?
provider_faqs.a: Hiscox writes general liability, professional liability (E&O), business owner's policies and cyber insurance for US small businesses. It says workers' compensation and some other coverage are available through partner carriers.

provider_faqs.q: How much does Hiscox cost?
provider_faqs.a: Hiscox quotes premiums per business. Get a quote online or through a broker and compare it with other carriers for the same limits.

provider_faqs.q: How is Hiscox different from ERGO NEXT?
provider_faqs.a: Both sell small-business insurance online. Hiscox writes general liability, professional liability, BOP and cyber itself and offers workers' comp through partner carriers; ERGO NEXT's company description lists general liability, BOP, workers' comp and professional liability. Get quotes from both for the same limits and compare the coverage, not only the price.

providers.name: Simply Business
providers.tagline: Online insurance marketplace owned by Travelers: one application, quotes from several carriers, buy online
providers.quote_speed: Online; Simply Business says you can compare quotes, buy and, for many policies, get a certificate of insurance within 10 minutes
providers.typical_premium_range: Quoted per business by each carrier on the panel
providers.states_note: Sold online across the US; confirm during the quote which carriers and coverages are offered for your trade in your state
providers.headquartered: London, UK (US office in Boston, MA; owned by Travelers since 2017)
providers.long_description:
Simply Business is an online insurance marketplace for small businesses, owned by Travelers since 2017. It started in the UK in 2005, and its offices include London and Northampton in the UK and Boston in the US; Simply Business, LLC, a Massachusetts company, is listed as a Travelers subsidiary in Travelers' 2025 annual report. Simply Business says it serves over one million active customers globally.

The model: you fill in one application, Simply Business matches your business with coverage from several carriers, and you compare the quotes, pick one and buy online. It says the US products include general liability, professional liability, business owner's policies (BOP), workers' compensation and cyber insurance. Travelers is on its carrier panel, and Simply Business has announced US partnerships with other carriers, including Employers for workers' comp (2024), Coterie for BOP (2024) and RLI for professional liability (2025).

Simply Business says that for many policies you can compare quotes, pay online and get your certificate of insurance within 10 minutes. In April 2026 it launched an app inside ChatGPT that gives a price estimate from three details (business type, estimated annual revenue and ZIP code) before you finish the quote on its website. It also works with independent agents: in December 2025 it announced a partnership with SIAA, an agency network, to give agents access to its products.

Because Simply Business is the agency, not the insurer, the carrier you pick issues the policy and pays claims. The Travelers ownership does not mean your policy is a Travelers policy; it depends on the quote you choose.

The trade-off: comparing several carriers in one place saves phone calls, but the quotes can differ in coverage as well as price, and the lines on offer center on liability, BOP, workers' comp and cyber. Check limits, exclusions and additional insured options on each quote, and confirm commercial auto or tools coverage separately if you need it.
providers.how_it_works: Fill in one online application about your business, such as your trade, location and the coverage you want. Simply Business matches you with quotes from carriers on its panel; compare them, pick one, pay online, and for many policies download your certificate of insurance straight away. You can also start with its ChatGPT app, which gives a price estimate from your business type, estimated annual revenue and ZIP code, then finish on the Simply Business website. The carrier you choose issues the policy and pays claims.

pros_detail.title: One application, several carriers
pros_detail.explanation: Simply Business matches your business with quotes from multiple carriers, so you can compare prices and coverage without calling several agents.

pros_detail.title: Fast online purchase and certificates
pros_detail.explanation: Simply Business says that for many policies you can compare, buy and get a certificate of insurance within 10 minutes.

pros_detail.title: Owned by Travelers
pros_detail.explanation: Travelers bought Simply Business in 2017, and Simply Business, LLC is listed as a Travelers subsidiary in Travelers' 2025 annual report.

pros_detail.title: Named carrier partners
pros_detail.explanation: Travelers is on the panel, and Simply Business has announced partnerships with Employers for workers' comp, Coterie for BOP and RLI for professional liability.

cons_detail.title: Quotes differ in coverage, not just price
cons_detail.explanation: Each quote comes from a different carrier with its own policy wording. Compare limits, exclusions and additional insured options, not only the premium.

cons_detail.title: Limited line-up for vehicle-heavy trades
cons_detail.explanation: The lines Simply Business names are general liability, professional liability, BOP, workers' comp and cyber. Shops that need commercial auto or tools coverage should confirm it during the quote or buy it elsewhere.

cons_detail.title: Claims go to the carrier
cons_detail.explanation: Simply Business is the agency; the carrier that issues your policy handles and pays claims, so the claims experience depends on which quote you pick.

cons_detail.title: Availability varies by trade and state
cons_detail.explanation: Which carriers and coverages you see depends on your business and location. Confirm the options for your trade in your state before relying on the comparison.

providers.best_for: Small trade businesses that want to compare quotes from several carriers for general liability, BOP, workers' comp or professional liability in one online application
providers.weaknesses: Quotes differ in coverage as well as price, commercial auto and tools coverage need checking separately, and claims are handled by whichever carrier issues the policy
providers.affiliate_payout_note: Direct publisher affiliate program with documented per-quote payouts (~$25-$40 range)

provider_faqs.q: Is Simply Business a carrier or a broker?
provider_faqs.a: It is an agency, not an insurer. Simply Business matches your business with quotes from multiple carriers; the carrier you choose issues the policy and pays claims.

provider_faqs.q: Who owns Simply Business?
provider_faqs.a: Travelers, which bought it in 2017. Simply Business started in the UK in 2005 and has a US office in Boston.

provider_faqs.q: Which carriers does Simply Business work with?
provider_faqs.a: Travelers is on its carrier panel, and Simply Business has announced US partnerships with Employers (workers' comp), Coterie (BOP) and RLI (professional liability), among others. The carriers you see depend on your trade and state.

provider_faqs.q: How is Simply Business different from ERGO NEXT?
provider_faqs.a: ERGO NEXT is an insurer that sells its own policies. Simply Business is an agency that shows quotes from several carriers in one place. If you want to compare carriers, Simply Business does that for you; if you want one insurer, you can go direct.

provider_faqs.q: What coverage can I buy?
provider_faqs.a: Simply Business lists general liability, professional liability, business owner's policies, workers' compensation and cyber insurance for US small businesses. Confirm commercial auto or tools coverage during the quote if you need it.

providers.name: Insureon
providers.tagline: Online insurance agency owned by Hub International since 2022: one application, quotes from several carriers, licensed agents on call
providers.quote_speed: Free online application; Insureon says coverage can start in less than 24 hours
providers.typical_premium_range: Quoted per business; Insureon's site shows average costs for contractor policies, but your price depends on trade, location, payroll, vehicles and claims history
providers.states_note: Hub International said in 2022 that Insureon served customers in all 50 states
providers.long_description:
Insureon is an online insurance agency for small businesses, based in Chicago. It does not write policies itself: you fill out one online application, Insureon shows quotes from the insurance companies it works with, and you buy the policy online. Insureon says its carriers include Hiscox, Travelers, Chubb and The Hartford, and that its licensed agents can help with limits, endorsements and harder-to-place risks.

Ownership changed in March 2022, when the broker Hub International bought the Insureon agency and brand and Bold Penguin bought its technology platform. At Hub, Insureon sits inside Specialty Program Group. When the deal was announced, Hub said Insureon served more than 350,000 small-business customers in all 50 states.

For trades, Insureon has contractor pages for general liability, workers' compensation, commercial auto, tools and equipment coverage, umbrella policies and business owner's policies (BOPs), and it publishes average cost figures for these lines. Your actual premium is quoted per business and depends on your trade, location, payroll, vehicles and claims history.

The trade-off: Insureon is an agency, so claims are handled by the carrier that issued your policy, and the quotes you see depend on which carriers on its panel will write your trade in your state. Comparing its quotes with a local independent agent or a direct carrier before you buy is worth the time.
providers.how_it_works: Fill out Insureon's free online application with basic details about your business, review the quotes that come back from carriers on its panel, then choose a policy and pay online. Insureon says coverage can start in less than 24 hours and you can get a certificate of insurance once you buy. Licensed agents are available if you need help. Insureon is your agency; claims are filed with the carrier that issued the policy.

pros_detail.title: One application, several carriers
pros_detail.explanation: Insureon's online application returns quotes from multiple carriers, which it says include Hiscox, Travelers, Chubb and The Hartford, so you can compare without filling out separate forms.

pros_detail.title: Covers the main contractor lines
pros_detail.explanation: Insureon's contractor pages cover general liability, workers' comp, commercial auto, tools and equipment, umbrella and BOPs, so a small trade shop can shop these lines in one place.

pros_detail.title: Licensed agents available
pros_detail.explanation: Insureon says its licensed agents can help you choose limits, add endorsements or find coverage for unusual risks, so you are not left alone with the form.

pros_detail.title: Part of a large broker
pros_detail.explanation: Hub International has owned the Insureon agency and brand since 2022, so the agency is backed by a large, established insurance broker.

cons_detail.title: Not the insurer
cons_detail.explanation: Insureon is an agency. Claims and coverage decisions sit with the carrier that issues your policy, so check which company that is before you buy.

cons_detail.title: Choice limited to its carrier panel
cons_detail.explanation: You only see quotes from carriers on Insureon's panel that will write your trade in your state. A local independent agent may have access to other companies.

cons_detail.title: No fixed published prices
cons_detail.explanation: Premiums are quoted per business. The average costs on Insureon's site are a starting point, not the price you will pay.

providers.best_for: Small trade businesses that want to compare quotes from several carriers online and buy without meeting an agent in person
providers.weaknesses: An agency, not an insurer: claims go to the issuing carrier, choice is limited to carriers on its panel, and prices are quoted rather than published
providers.affiliate_payout_note: Affiliate program exists but documented payout terms unclear; outreach required

provider_faqs.q: Who owns Insureon?
provider_faqs.a: Hub International bought the Insureon agency and brand in March 2022, and Bold Penguin bought Insureon's technology platform in the same deal. Insureon is part of Hub's Specialty Program Group.

provider_faqs.q: Is Insureon an insurance company?
provider_faqs.a: No. Insureon is a licensed insurance agency. It shows quotes from carriers on its panel, and the policy you buy is issued by one of those carriers, which also handles your claims.

providers.name: Thimble
providers.tagline: Digital MGA owned by Arch Insurance since 2023: liability coverage by the job, month or year, bought online, in its app or by phone
providers.quote_speed: Online, in the app or by phone; coverage can start the same day you buy
providers.typical_premium_range: Quoted per job, month or year
providers.states_note: Thimble says it offers small business liability insurance across the United States; check its availability page for your state and trade
providers.long_description:
Thimble sells short-term and annual liability insurance for small businesses on its website, in its app and by phone. You can buy coverage by the job (down to hours or days), by the month or by the year, which suits trades with irregular or seasonal work, or a single job that needs a certificate of insurance before you start.

Thimble is not an insurance company. It is a digital managing general agent (MGA) that arranges policies with carrier partners; at the time of its 2023 sale those partners included Markel and Employers. Arch Insurance, part of Arch Capital Group, acquired Thimble in April 2023, and Thimble kept selling under its own brand. When the deal was announced, Thimble had delivered more than 170,000 policies. The company started as Verifly, an on-demand drone insurance startup, and rebranded to Thimble in 2019.

Thimble's site lists general liability, professional liability, business equipment protection, business owner's policies (BOPs), cyber and event insurance. Commercial auto is not on that list. In 2026 Thimble announced a WTW-built pricing engine and a ChatGPT integration that lets brokers and partners generate quotes.

The trade-off: short policies are handy for one-off jobs, but they end when the job window ends and have to be bought again. Trades with work vehicles need a separate auto policy, and if you work year-round it is worth comparing an annual Thimble policy against annual quotes from other carriers.
providers.how_it_works: Choose the coverage you need, enter your trade and business details, and pick the length: by the job (hours or days), the month or the year. You can buy on Thimble's website, in its app or over the phone, and coverage can start the same day. Thimble arranges the policy with one of its carrier partners and you can download proof of coverage after you buy. Job-length policies end when the chosen window ends.

pros_detail.title: Coverage by the job, month or year
pros_detail.explanation: You can match coverage to the work: a policy for a single job, a monthly policy for a busy season, or an annual policy.

pros_detail.title: Buy online, in the app or by phone
pros_detail.explanation: Thimble sells directly through its website, its app and over the phone, and coverage can start the same day you buy.

pros_detail.title: Owned by Arch
pros_detail.explanation: Arch Insurance, part of Arch Capital Group, has owned Thimble since 2023, and Thimble has kept launching products since the deal.

cons_detail.title: Not an insurance company
cons_detail.explanation: Thimble is an MGA and the policy is issued by a carrier partner. Check which carrier is named on your policy documents.

cons_detail.title: No commercial auto
cons_detail.explanation: Commercial auto is not among the lines Thimble lists, so trades with work vehicles need a separate auto policy.

cons_detail.title: Short policies need rebuying
cons_detail.explanation: Job-length coverage ends when the job window does. If you forget to buy the next policy, you are uninsured for that work.

providers.best_for: Solo trades and small crews with irregular, seasonal or one-off jobs that need liability coverage or a certificate of insurance quickly
providers.weaknesses: An MGA rather than the insurer, no commercial auto on its product list, and short-term policies must be bought again for each job or period
providers.affiliate_payout_note: Affiliate program exists but documented terms unclear

provider_faqs.q: Who owns Thimble?
provider_faqs.a: Arch Insurance, part of Arch Capital Group, acquired Thimble in April 2023. Thimble still sells under its own name; it arranges policies with carrier partners rather than issuing them itself.

provider_faqs.q: Can I buy insurance for just one job?
provider_faqs.a: Yes. Thimble sells coverage by the job, the month or the year, and job-length coverage can be as short as hours or days. The policy ends when the window you chose ends.

providers.name: The Hartford
providers.tagline: Hartford, Connecticut insurer dating to 1810 that sells small business policies online, by phone and through independent agents
providers.quote_speed: Online, by phone or through an independent agent
providers.typical_premium_range: Quoted per business
providers.states_note: The Hartford sells small business insurance across the US; coverages and eligibility vary by state and type of business
providers.long_description:
The Hartford is an insurer based in Hartford, Connecticut, with a history going back to 1810. Its parent company trades on the New York Stock Exchange as HIG and changed its legal name from The Hartford Financial Services Group to Hartford Insurance Group in 2025. Besides small business insurance, it sells personal insurance and group benefits.

For contractors, The Hartford sells business owner's policies (BOPs, which combine general liability, commercial property and business income coverage), general liability, workers' compensation, commercial auto and professional liability. The Hartford says most contracting businesses have a BOP.

You can get a quote online, by phone or through an independent agent. Your actual premium is quoted per business and depends on your trade, location, payroll, vehicles and claims history.

The trade-off: buying direct shows you only The Hartford's price. An independent agent who writes The Hartford can compare it with other carriers, which is the only way to know whether its quote is competitive for your trade.
providers.how_it_works: Start a quote on The Hartford's website or by phone, entering details about your business, trade, payroll and vehicles. You can also buy The Hartford through an independent agent. The Hartford is the insurer, so it issues the policy and handles claims.

pros_detail.title: Long-established insurer
pros_detail.explanation: The Hartford dates to 1810 and says it has more than 200 years of experience. Its parent is a publicly traded company (NYSE: HIG).

pros_detail.title: Several ways to buy
pros_detail.explanation: You can get a quote online, by phone or through an independent agent, whichever suits you.

pros_detail.title: Main contractor lines in one place
pros_detail.explanation: BOP, general liability, workers' comp, commercial auto and professional liability can all sit with one carrier.

cons_detail.title: Quoted prices only
cons_detail.explanation: Beyond an advertised starting price, premiums are quoted per business, so you need a quote to compare.

cons_detail.title: One carrier's price when buying direct
cons_detail.explanation: Online and phone quotes show only The Hartford's price. To compare, use an independent agent or a multi-carrier broker.

cons_detail.title: Eligibility varies

Travelers sells business insurance through independent agents and brokers. It runs a unit for small businesses, generally those with fewer than 50 employees, that offers package policies (commercial multi-peril, similar to a BOP), workers' compensation, commercial auto, general liability and commercial property.

Travelers also owns Simply Business, an online small business insurance broker it bought in 2017. Simply Business, LLC is listed as a Travelers subsidiary in its annual report for 2025, and it operates under its own brand.

Liberty Mutual is a Boston-based insurer, founded in 1912, that sells both personal and business insurance. For small businesses it offers business owner's policies (BOPs), general liability, workers' compensation, commercial auto and other coverages. You can start online on its small business pages or buy through a local independent agent who writes Liberty Mutual.

The commercial side is split by account size. Liberty Mutual's mid-size to large commercial and specialty business sits in a unit called Global Risk Solutions, which has a construction industry practice and offers lines such as commercial auto and fleet, general liability, workers' comp, umbrella and excess, inland marine and surety.

Liberty Mutual says it has been in the insurance business for more than 100 years. It does not publish small business premiums; your price is quoted based on your trade, location, payroll, vehicles and claims history.

The trade-off: Liberty Mutual can insure anything from a small trade shop to a large contractor, but the only way to know whether it is competitive for you is to compare its quote with others, ideally through an independent agent who can shop several carriers at once.

providers.long_description:
Erie Insurance (ERIE) is a regional property and casualty insurer founded in 1925 and based in Erie, Pennsylvania. The insurer, Erie Insurance Exchange, is a reciprocal owned by its policyholders (called subscribers). Erie Indemnity Company has managed the Exchange as its attorney-in-fact since 1925 and is paid a management fee capped at 25% of the premiums the Exchange writes, according to its 2025 annual report. ERIE says it has nearly seven million policies in force.

For trade businesses, ERIE's 2025 annual report names commercial multi-peril (package) policies, commercial auto and workers' compensation as its main commercial products; commercial lines made up 29% of the Exchange's 2025 written premium. ERIE's website also has pages for general liability, commercial property, surety bonds and cyber coverage, and an industry page for contractors.

ERIE sells only through independent agencies, which its annual report calls the Exchange's sole distribution channel, so there is no online quote-and-buy option. It operates in 12 states and Washington, DC: Illinois, Indiana, Kentucky, Maryland, New York, North Carolina, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Tennessee, Virginia, West Virginia and Wisconsin. A contractor based elsewhere cannot buy from ERIE.

The trade-off: you need a business inside ERIE's footprint and a local independent agent, and ERIE does not publish commercial prices. The only way to judge its price is to have your agent quote ERIE next to the other carriers that agent represents.
providers.how_it_works: Find an independent insurance agency that represents ERIE in your state. The agent collects your business details (trade, payroll, vehicles, revenue and the coverage you need) and requests an ERIE quote. Independent agents usually represent more than one carrier, so ask for other quotes at the same time. If you buy, the agent binds the policy and handles service such as certificates of insurance and policy changes, and ERIE handles the claims.

providers.long_description:
Pie Insurance is a small-business insurer founded in 2017 that focuses on workers' compensation. Its workers' comp policies are underwritten by its own insurance company, The Pie Insurance Company (NAIC 21857), and affiliates, and sold by its licensed agency, Pie Insurance Services, Inc. In January 2026 Pie said it had more than 55,000 policies in force in 39 states and Washington, DC, worked with more than 5,000 agencies and had raised more than $615 million since 2017.

For trade businesses, the core product is workers' comp, which Pie says you can quote online in about three minutes, or through a partner agency. Pie advertises workers' comp savings of up to 30% and offers pay-as-you-go billing, where the monthly premium is based on actual payroll coordinated with your payroll provider instead of an up-front estimate. It also sells general liability, business owner's policies, commercial auto and professional liability, which its legal page says are underwritten by third-party insurers.

As Pie's own workers' comp page explains, a standard policy is priced on estimated payroll and checked by a premium audit after the policy period ends, so a business whose payroll grew can owe more. Pie's BBB profile (Pie Insurance Services, Washington, DC) showed no accreditation and 15 complaints closed in the last three years when checked on September 30, 2026. In May 2024 Florida's insurance regulator fined two Pie insurers a combined $21,750 for filing required data late.

The trade-off: Pie is a quick way to get an online workers' comp quote in most states, with a pay-as-you-go option that can reduce audit surprises, but see the reputation warning. Read the complaints on bbb.org, ask how the year-end audit and disputes work, and compare quotes from other carriers before you buy.
providers.how_it_works: Enter your business type, trade and payroll estimate on Pie's website, or go through an agency that works with Pie, and get a workers' comp quote, which Pie says takes about 3 minutes. You can pay a standard premium based on estimated payroll or choose pay-as-you-go billing, where the monthly premium follows your actual payroll through your payroll provider. After the policy period ends, Pie runs a premium audit that compares actual payroll with the estimate. General liability, BOP, commercial auto and professional liability are sold by Pie's agency and underwritten by third-party insurers.

Because biBERK is an insurer selling its own policies rather than a broker, you get one set of products and one underwriting appetite. If biBERK does not write your trade or prices it high, it will not shop other insurers for you, so a broker quote is a useful comparison.

Huckleberry is an online small-business insurance agency. It now operates as Huckleberry by Paychex, which its website describes as the digital quoting and binding tool of Paychex Insurance Agency, Inc. Huckleberry is not an insurer: you fill in one online application, it gets quotes from partner insurance carriers, and you can compare them and buy the same day, with the policy written by the carrier you choose.

Huckleberry says most customers can get a quote in about five minutes. Its site covers workers' compensation, general liability, business owner's policies, professional liability, commercial auto, business property and umbrella coverage, and it has industry pages for trades such as electricians, HVAC, plumbing, painters, carpenters, landscaping, cleaning and pressure washing. It says it can quote in all 50 states and Washington, DC, though the coverage types available vary by state.

Because Huckleberry is an agency, the claims handling and financial strength behind your policy come from the carrier it places you with. When an insurer wants to look at an application more closely, Huckleberry says the usual turnaround is the same business day. For small businesses, Chubb offers a business owner's policy for companies with up to $30 million in revenue in more than 500 business classes, and it names artisan contractors among the eligible industries. The BOP combines property and liability coverage, with options such as data breach, employment practices liability and crime, and Chubb suggests pairing it with workers' compensation, commercial auto, umbrella and cyber coverage. Its small-business workers' comp covers businesses with as little as one employee and up to $30 million in revenue.

You can request a quote on Chubb's website or buy through an independent agent or broker. For workers' comp claims, Chubb says it offers online claims reporting, contacts you within 24 hours on lost-time claims, and uses in-house nurse case managers and return-to-work programs.

providers.long_description:
Progressive Commercial is the business insurance arm of The Progressive Corporation (NYSE: PGR), which was founded in 1937 and is headquartered in Mayfield Village, Ohio. Its lead product is commercial auto. Progressive says it has more than 50 years of experience in commercial insurance, and it insures business cars, pickups, vans, SUVs, box trucks, dump trucks, tow trucks, semis and trailers, with liability, collision, comprehensive, uninsured/underinsured motorist and medical payments coverage.

Beyond vehicles, Progressive Commercial sells a business owner's policy (liability plus property), general liability, professional liability, workers' compensation and cyber insurance. Progressive discloses that these non-auto policies are underwritten by insurers affiliated with Progressive and by unaffiliated insurers, that Progressive Advantage Agency, Inc. tries to quote each applicant with at least one of them, and that each insurer is solely responsible for its own claims. A contractor who bundles auto with a BOP can therefore end up with two different insurance companies on the paperwork.

Prices are quoted per business, but Progressive publishes 2025 figures for new customers. Contractors such as carpenters, electricians, landscapers and painters paid a median of $203 a month (average $260) per vehicle for liability and physical damage coverage, and a BOP had a national median of $80 a month (average $127). Listed commercial auto discounts include bundling a BOP or general liability policy, continuous prior coverage, paying in full, and enrolling in Snapshot ProView. You can quote online, by phone or through an independent agent.

The trade-off: Progressive's core is vehicles. It does not write commercial auto in Washington, D.C., does not offer business insurance in Hawaii, and BOP availability varies by state. For the non-auto lines you are buying through Progressive's agency from whichever insurer it places you with, so check the insurer named on each policy and compare the package with an independent agent at renewal.

Commercial auto is written by Progressive's insurance companies. For a BOP, general liability, professional liability or workers' comp, Progressive Advantage Agency tries to quote you with at least one of its affiliated or unaffiliated insurers, and the insurer that issues each policy handles its claims. Nationwide sells business insurance through independent agents and points buyers to its agent locator. That suits a contractor who wants an agent to assess the trade, payroll, vehicles and exposures, put the package together and handle certificates and renewals. Markel is a specialty insurer and the insurance business of Markel Group Inc. (NYSE: MKL), headquartered in Glen Allen, Virginia. Its history goes back to 1930, when Sam Markel began insuring jitney buses. The holding company, called Markel Corp until 2023, also owns non-insurance businesses. In 2025 it sold the renewal rights of its reinsurance operations to focus on specialty insurance.

For trades, Markel sells both admitted coverage (workers' comp, general liability, commercial property) and non-admitted excess and surplus (E&S) lines, including small business casualty and property, excess casualty and contractors' pollution. Its commercial and residential services pages name artisan contractors such as electricians, fence contractors, lawn sprinkler installers and carpet cleaners, along with janitorial, lawn care and pest control businesses. Its construction pages add inland marine and large builders risk and describe clients from small artisan contractors to large infrastructure projects.

Markel Surety writes contract bonds (bid, performance and payment) and commercial bonds. Markel says its main contract surety appetite is preferred, high-quality contractors, with capacity up to $500 million, and it also offers the SBA Surety Guarantee Program, funds disbursement and collateralized options. Bond applications are submitted by agents appointed with Markel Surety.

The trade-off: Markel is sold through agents and brokers, not direct, so you need an agent with access to Markel's portals or appointment. Pricing is quoted by its underwriters and not published, and E&S coverage is non-admitted, so check the policy terms and your state's rules with your broker. For a simple, low-hazard trade, a standard small-business carrier may be quicker to buy.

Cerity launched in January 2019, first in Illinois, as an online platform for small business owners and freelancers. Its policies are written by EMPLOYERS insurance companies, including Cerity Insurance Company.

The pitch is buying workers' comp online without an agent. EMPLOYERS describes Cerity as digital-first, direct-to-consumer workers' comp with fast and affordable coverage through an online platform, and its 10-K says Cerity specializes in smaller risks in classes where customers prefer to buy online. At launch, Cerity said it quoted in seconds, issued policies in under five minutes and used a pricing model with up to 100 price points; its current site could not be read to confirm those figures today.

Cerity is a workers' comp product only. EMPLOYERS' filings describe it as direct-to-customer workers' comp and do not list general liability, a BOP or commercial auto, so a trades business will buy those lines elsewhere. EMPLOYERS writes workers' comp throughout the US apart from four states where coverage comes only from a state fund.

The trade-off: you get a quick, self-serve way to meet a workers' comp requirement from a workers' comp specialist, but no agent to advise you and no other business lines. CNA describes itself as one of the largest U.S. commercial property and casualty insurers.

For contractors, CNA has a dedicated construction team and names classes such as electrical, roofing, concrete, grading and excavation, general contractors, and sheet metal, mechanical, A/C and plumbing. Its small business BOP, CNA Connect, offers property and general liability for more than 600 classes of business and automatically includes blanket additional insured status with products-completed operations coverage for contractors. CNA also writes workers' comp, commercial auto, umbrella and excess, professional and pollution liability, builders risk and cyber, and larger contractors can use its CNA Paramount package.

CNA sells only through independent agents and brokers. Agents quote and bind small business policies on its CNA Central platform, and CNA says 80% of small business classes are issued in real time, with most others within two hours. It also offers construction risk-control resources, including PrepWise and SORCE for Construction.

The trade-off: you cannot buy CNA directly, prices are quoted rather than published, and the experience depends on the agent who places and services your policy. A contractor that wants an insurer with contractor-specific BOP terms and room to add workers' comp, auto and umbrella can ask an agent to quote CNA.

Coterie Insurance is a small-business insurance platform that launched in 2018 and is now headquartered in Appleton, Wisconsin, operating as a fully digital, remote-friendly company. It is a licensed insurance agency rather than an insurer: Coterie says its policies are backed by licensed insurers and reinsurers, and it offers admitted products in all 50 states. Its products are a business owner's policy (BOP), general liability, professional liability, cyber, employment practices liability and workplace violence coverage.

Coterie's model runs through intermediaries. It works through insurance agents and brokers, digital partner platforms that embed its quotes through an API, and networks, aggregators and wholesalers, and it points business owners to a 'Find an Agent' tool. Coterie says it produces instant bindable quotes and has an appetite for more than 80% of small businesses.

For trades, the BOP combines general liability, commercial property and business interruption and can be paid monthly or annually. Contractors face tighter limits than other businesses: Coterie's BOP is open to contractors with up to 15 employees and $5 million in annual revenue, against 50 employees and $10 million for other small businesses. Coterie does not list workers' comp or commercial auto.

The trade-off: Coterie can get a small contractor a quick BOP or general liability policy through an agent or partner, but it covers only part of a trades business's needs, it does not name the insurers behind its policies on its site, and larger contractors fall outside its BOP limits. Ask your agent which insurer issues the policy and pair it with separate workers' comp and commercial auto.

Policies are issued by the licensed insurers that back Coterie, and BOPs can be paid monthly or annually.

Selective Insurance is a property and casualty insurer founded in 1926 in Branchville, New Jersey, as Selected Risks Insurance Company. In 2026, its 100th year, it opened a new corporate headquarters in Short Hills, New Jersey. Selective describes itself as a holding company for 10 property and casualty insurance companies, and it sells through independent agents rather than directly to businesses.

Contractors are one of the industries Selective names on its business insurance pages. Its contractors page covers general, heavy and trade contractors, including carpenters, electricians and commercial roofers. The core coverages listed are general liability with blanket additional insured for ongoing and completed operations, commercial auto, inland marine (builders risk, contractor's equipment and installation floaters) and commercial property. Workers compensation, surety bonds, cyber liability, employment practices liability and management liability are listed as add-ons. Selective also offers a business owners policy and a commercial umbrella that it says starts at $1 million and goes up to $25 million.

Selective lists risk control services for contractors, including best-practices assessments, contractual liability consultation, workers compensation cost containment, driver and fleet safety programs, and OSHA 30-hour training. For harder-to-place risks, its affiliate Mesa Underwriters Specialty Insurance Company (MUSIC) writes excess and surplus lines business in all 50 states through wholesale general agents.

Standard business coverage is available only in the states Selective lists: 36 states and the District of Columbia as of September 2026. California, Texas and Florida are not among them, so contractors there cannot buy a standard Selective policy.

The trade-off: Selective is reached only through an independent agent, it does not publish premiums, and its standard commercial footprint leaves out several large states. For contractors in its states who want an agent-placed program with contractor risk control services, it is worth asking an agent to quote.
providers.how_it_works: Selective sells business insurance through independent agents, and its site has an agent locator. The agent gathers details on your trade, payroll, vehicles, equipment and projects, then quotes coverage such as general liability, commercial auto, inland marine, commercial property, workers compensation, a business owners policy, a commercial umbrella and surety bonds. The agent handles binding, certificates and service. Contractors with complex or high-hazard exposures may instead be placed with Selective's E&S affiliate MUSIC through a wholesale general agent. Farmers Insurance is a group of insurers that sells auto, home and small business insurance. It was founded in 1928, and its home office is in Los Angeles (its press releases are datelined Woodland Hills, a Los Angeles neighborhood). Its three main insurers, Farmers Insurance Exchange, Fire Insurance Exchange and Truck Insurance Exchange, are California interinsurance exchanges owned by their policyholders. Farmers Group, Inc., a wholly owned subsidiary of Swiss-based Zurich Insurance Group, acts as their attorney-in-fact and provides non-claims services for a fee. Zurich says it has no ownership interest in the Exchanges themselves. Farmers says Farmers Insurance Exchange is on the 2026 Fortune 500 list.

For contractors, Farmers says it makes it easy for plumbers, electricians, landscapers and other contractors to get the coverage they want in a single, easy-to-manage policy. Its business pages cover a business owners policy (liability and property coverage that can be customized), general liability (which Farmers says is standard on all its business policies), commercial auto and workers compensation.

Coverage is sold through Farmers agents, and Farmers points out that its agents are small business owners themselves. An owner who already has a car or home insured through a Farmers agent can ask the same agent to quote business coverage. Premiums are quoted per account, and Farmers says not all products, coverages or features are available in every state.

The trade-off: Farmers sells small business insurance alongside its auto and home lines rather than running a construction specialty program, pricing is only available through an agent quote, and what you can buy depends on your state. Contractors with high-hazard work or large projects should also get quotes from carriers with dedicated construction programs.

providers.long_description:
Berkshire Hathaway GUARD Insurance Companies is a property and casualty insurance group based in Wilkes-Barre, Pennsylvania. Berkshire Hathaway acquired it through National Indemnity Company in late 2012; Warren Buffett's 2012 shareholder letter described Guard as a Wilkes-Barre company that writes workers compensation insurance, primarily for smaller businesses. It took the Berkshire Hathaway GUARD name in 2013. Berkshire's 2025 annual report says GUARD primarily offers commercial insurance products to small and medium-sized businesses and sells through independent agents, wholesale brokers and managing general agents.

GUARD's product pages include a businessowners policy (property and liability bundled in one policy), workers compensation, commercial auto, commercial umbrella liability and excess and surplus lines coverage, and it has an industry page for artisan contractors. For a small trades shop, that means one agent can place workers comp, a BOP, vehicles and an umbrella with the same carrier.

GUARD has also been shrinking. Berkshire reported that GUARD's written premiums fell 16.3% in 2024 and 32.6% in 2025 as it exited unprofitable lines and tightened underwriting standards, with lower volume in personal lines, businessowners and workers compensation business. providers.long_description:
AmTrust Financial Services is a property and casualty insurer headquartered in New York. It began in 1998 (it marked its 20th anniversary in 2018) and describes itself as a multinational insurer specializing in coverage for small businesses, with an emphasis on workers' compensation. AmTrust has been privately held since November 29, 2018, when Barry Zyskind, George Karfunkel, Leah Karfunkel and funds managed by Stone Point Capital completed a go-private transaction and its Nasdaq trading ended.

For a trades business, AmTrust's relevance is small business workers' compensation. Its small business product pages list workers' compensation, a businessowners policy (which bundles general liability, property and business interruption), package policies, employment practices liability and cyber coverage. Coverage is sold through insurance agents, and premiums are quoted per account.

In June 2020 the SEC charged AmTrust and its former CFO with failing to disclose material facts about how the company estimated insurance losses and reserves. Without admitting or denying the allegations, AmTrust agreed to a permanent injunction and a $10.3 million penalty. More recently, in December 2025, AmTrust and Blackstone Credit & Insurance moved seven AmTrust specialty MGAs into a new company, ANV Group Holdings, with AmTrust continuing to underwrite those books under a ten-year capacity agreement.

The trade-off: AmTrust is built around small business workers' comp, but you reach it through an agent, prices are quoted per account, and its record includes a 2020 SEC settlement over loss-reserve disclosures. Have your agent compare its workers' comp quote with other carriers.

The agent handles binding, certificates and policy service. Premiums are quoted per account.

providers.long_description:
State Farm is a mutual insurer headquartered in Bloomington, Illinois. Its parent, State Farm Mutual Automobile Insurance Company, is a mutual company whose members are its policyholders, and State Farm says it has been in business for over 100 years (it was founded in 1922). State Farm says its companies are the largest providers of auto and home insurance combined in the United States, with more than 19,200 agent offices and over 62,000 employees, and it sells commercial policies and business owners coverage alongside its personal lines.

For trades, State Farm sells a contractors policy (its site refers to Artisan and Service Contractors policies). Its contractors page names electricians, plumbers and landscapers and lists business personal property, building property, liability, completed operations, property of others and installation floater coverage, with tools and equipment coverage as an option. Workers' compensation and commercial auto are separate policies, and State Farm's small business lineup also includes a business owners policy, a commercial liability umbrella, professional liability, employment practices liability, inland marine and surety and fidelity bonds.

Coverage is sold through local State Farm agents, who work as independent contractor agents. Contractors and workers' compensation policies require a final premium audit after the policy period, which reviews your actual payroll or the cost of work your subcontractors completed, so the final premium can differ from the estimate. State Farm's contractors pages do not list which trades or contractor types qualify, so confirm eligibility for your work with an agent.

State Farm also faces legal and regulatory scrutiny over its handling of claims from the January 2025 Los Angeles wildfires. Los Angeles County sued it on August 31, 2026, and according to the county, the California Department of Insurance reported 398 violations in a review of 220 claims.

The trade-off: State Farm offers a broad small business lineup and a local agent, which suits owners who already insure a home or vehicles with State Farm, but you must go through an agent, premiums are quoted per account and audited for contractors, and eligibility for your specific trade needs to be confirmed up front.
providers.how_it_works: State Farm business insurance is sold through local State Farm agents; you can find one by ZIP code or ask an agent to contact you through statefarm.com. The agent reviews your trade, payroll, vehicles and equipment and quotes a contractors policy or business owners policy plus any workers' compensation, commercial auto or umbrella coverage you need. Contractors and workers' compensation policies are audited after the policy period to settle the final premium based on actual payroll or subcontractor costs. The same agent can also handle your personal auto and home policies.

providers.long_description:
Zurich North America, headquartered in Schaumburg, Illinois, is the North American business of Zurich Insurance Group, which was founded in 1872. Zurich says its US business serves over 90% of the Fortune 500 and employs nearly 9,000 people in the United States. In January 2025 it grouped its Construction, Surety and Financial Lines businesses into a new Specialties business unit.

Construction is one of Zurich's specialty businesses. Zurich says it has served construction customers for more than 25 years and has nearly 100 construction risk engineers. Its construction offering includes builders risk, casualty coverage, professional liability and contract surety bonds. In August 2025 it launched a Fronted Master Builders Risk program for owners and contractors with pipelines of large projects, which it says is ideal for projects over $250 million and has supported over $80 billion in insurable values. In December 2025 it added a builders risk product for data center projects, available from January 2026 on a project-specific, non-admitted basis.

Zurich pairs coverage with risk engineering. It has piloted construction fleet video telematics and uses camera-enabled coaching on large jobsites; Zurich says a pilot across nine New York projects valued at over $2 billion cut workers' compensation claim frequency by more than 50 percent before it made the program available nationwide in late 2025.

Zurich's construction materials focus on large projects, owners and contractors, and its programs are placed through brokers. A small trades shop looking for a quick small business policy should look at small business carriers and brokers instead.

The trade-off: Zurich brings large-project builders risk, casualty and surety capacity plus risk engineering, but it works only through brokers, pricing is set per account or project, and its offering is aimed at large construction rather than small service trades.
providers.how_it_works: Zurich's construction coverage is placed through insurance brokers. A broker with construction experience submits your company or project details (operations, payroll, fleet, project values and contracts) to Zurich's construction underwriters, who can quote builders risk, casualty, professional liability or contract surety, often alongside risk engineering services. Some products, such as Zurich's data center builders risk, are written on a project-specific, non-admitted basis. The broker manages placement and service, and pricing is quoted per account or project.
